title: How to contain shadow AI, as it takes on multiple forms and spreads throughout your environment
description: Shadow AI refers to the unauthorized and ungoverned use of AI tools and models within enterprise environments, spanning from simple chatbots to complex autonomous agents and local AI models. This phenomenon has grown significantly, creating blind spots in security and increasing risks such as data loss, operational disruption, and regulatory fines. Shadow AI incidents have more than doubled recently, with associated breach costs exceeding the global average. Enterprises face challenges detecting and controlling shadow AI due to its diverse forms and rapid adoption outpacing governance. Mitigation involves employee training, establishing AI usage policies, and integrating shadow AI management into exposure management programs.
aiSummary: Shadow AI encompasses a wide range of unsanctioned AI assets and activities within organizations, including unvetted AI servers, browser extensions, local AI models, autonomous agents, and AI coding assistants. These tools often operate without IT or security department knowledge, leading to significant security blind spots. Examples include employees sharing sensitive data with public AI tools, installing unauthorized AI infrastructure, and granting AI agents broad access to private data. According to IBM's 2026 Cost of a Data Breach Report, shadow AI-related security incidents have increased from 20% to 43%, with an average breach cost of $5.39 million. The Cloud Security Alliance highlights that AI adoption has outpaced governance, resulting in an invisible AI infrastructure layer lacking policy enforcement and audits. Detection tools like Tenable One have identified millions of AI-related exposures, underscoring the scale of the problem. Effective mitigation requires awareness training, clear AI acceptable use policies, and unified exposure management.
aiImpact: Shadow AI incidents have led to significant impacts including data loss or compromise in nearly half of cases, operational disruptions in 42%, and regulatory fines in 21%. The average cost of a shadow AI-related data breach is approximately $5.39 million, which is about $400,000 higher than the global average. The proliferation of unsanctioned AI tools creates security blind spots, increases risk of intellectual property leakage, and complicates compliance efforts. The rapid and ungoverned adoption of AI tools exposes enterprises to elevated risks across data privacy, operational continuity, and regulatory compliance.
